_note: Hand-pinned resolutions, consulted by harvest-sparql.js at the moment it picks
a Wikidata item for a seed line. Key = the seed line, lowercased, exactly as it
appears in seeds.txt. Value = the QID that line means.
An override only ever selects among the candidates the resolve query already
returned; it cannot invent a film. If it matches nothing the run warns and falls
through to the ranked pick, so a stale pin degrades to the default rather than
poisoning a key with a label-less QID.
Two entries below are corrections to films the OLD unordered pick got wrong and
shipped: corpus.json holds Q12280475 (a 1930 Macedonian short) under 'earth' and
Q17498893 (Chang Cheh's The Duel) under 'the duel'. Measured against live WDQS on
2026-08-08, the deterministic ranking now reaches both of these on its own --
Q55188 wins on the en.wikipedia sitelink, Q583407 wins on the exact rdfs:label --
so these pins are belt-and-braces, not the mechanism. They are here because
Wikidata is mutable: the day Q12280475 gains a sitelink, the ranking flips back,
and this corpus has already carried the wrong Earth through two generations.
